phase3_findings.description: Operand-confirmation guard (skills/create-issue/SKILL.md lines 201-204) says each peer must 'confirm the leg's operand', which can be read as presence-only (the return merely states some --search-space value) rather than a value-match of the returned operand against the pathspec the orchestrator dispatched. Under the presence-only reading a peer that silently defaulted its search-space but echoes back a --search-space value would read as 'confirmed', escaping the unestablished/breadcrumb path — so the guarantee 'a peer that silently defaulted the operand is detected, not trusted' is not fully delivered. Tighten the wording to require the orchestrator to match the returned operand against the leg's resolved pathspec (value equality). Single-source; flagged as prose-clarity hardening, not a fail-open runtime defect.

fail_items.claim: The absolute guarantee 'a peer that silently defaulted the operand is detected, not trusted' (skills/create-issue/SKILL.md:201-204).
fail_items.evidence: The prose instructs each peer to STATE the --search-space operand it ran under and records a leg unestablished when a return 'does not confirm the leg's operand', but never instructs the orchestrator to compare the returned operand against the pathspec it dispatched (the value-match). Under a presence-only reading the guarantee is falsifiable, so the source-authored absolute claim overstates what the described mechanism achieves.
